messages:
Iris (PM): Quick sync — we need to finalize launch acceptance criteria and an explicit fallthrough plan for 1.2.0. Customer asks: max P95 latency 350ms for hosted tier. Can we commit?
Ben (Eng): 350ms P95 is tight for peak seq len 1024. We can hit it mostly with batching+kv cache, but error budget will spike if model cold starts.
Maya (SRE): FYI error budget for hosted is currently 10% monthly. If we take that SLA we need a hard degrade path at 5% burn.
Omar (ML): Options: quantized variant (faster, slight quality delta), or shorter context path (truncate/truncation policy). Both reduce cost/latency.
Iris (PM): For customers that opt-in to SLA, what's the recommended behavior when load threatens SLO? auto-fallback to quantized model or degrade features? Need tradeoffs listed in PRD acceptance.
Ben (Eng): Prefer model variant fallback + admission control. Flow: if P95 projection > threshold -> route new requests to quantized model; heavy requests get 429 + retry-after when sustained. That keeps correctness.
Maya (SRE): +1 for admission control. But 429s are bad for UX. Suggest a canary: fallback first to quantized, if quality drop > eval-threshold then enable token-limited responses.
Devin (DevEx): We should document exact signals and thresholds in the PRD. Suggest fields: "latency_projection_ms", "error_budget_burn_pct", "quality_regression_pct" and a playbook. Example config: 
```
fallback_policy: {
  latency_threshold_ms: 350,
  projection_window_s: 60,
  error_budget_burn_pct: 5,
  fallback_model: "gpt-like-q4_8bit",
  degrade_mode: "stream_trim"
}
```
Ben (Eng): Edge case: request with tool-calls or function-calling requires full model for correctness. We need blacklist rules to never fallback for those. Add to PRD acceptance criteria: "no fallback for requests with function:true".
Omar (ML): Also add eval set: a 200-sample prompt set per customer to measure quality drift on fallback variants. Acceptance: quality_regression_pct <= 2% (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval metric).
Iris (PM): Good — draft acceptance bullets so we can sign off: 1) P95 <= 350ms for 95% of daily windows OR automatic fallback triggers, 2) Fallback must not be applied to function-calls/tools, 3) Quality regression on fallback <=2% on customer eval set, 4) Error budget burn mitigation action within 5 minutes of detection.
Maya (SRE): Add rollout/monitoring: per-route realtime chart, alert on projection > 90% of threshold, automated canary (5% traffic) for any new fallback policy.
Ben (Eng): Implementation notes: need route-level config, asymmetric routing (hosted -> quantized), and a graceful token limiter when fallback fails. I'll add a small sequence diagram in PRD.
Devin (DevEx): I'll add example SDK behavior: client sees x-reason header when routed to fallback: "x-inference-fallback: quantized" and structured event to analytics.
Iris (PM): Action items: Ben + Omar draft PRD section for fallback + acceptance criteria by EOD Fri; Maya to outline alerting + playbook; Devin to document SDK surface. We'll review Mon morning.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: canary/fallback-policy/v1 -> staging at 1976543500 :rocket:
Ben (Eng): noted — will link PR with architecture diagram and sample config.
Maya (SRE): Thanks — also adding a short postmortem template in case fallback caused unexpected quality regressions so we can tie to regression alerts.
Iris (PM): Perfect. If anyone has strong objections to the 2% quality SLA, call it out now. Otherwise I'll fold these into the PRD and tag legal for SLA language. :thumbsup:
Omar (ML): 2% seems reasonable for most customers; for top-tier we can offer configurable strictness.
Ben (Eng): no objections.
Devin (DevEx): ok. I'll start draft samples and an FAQ for customers.
Iris (PM): Great — closing thread, will post PRD link when draft ready.
